steps.system_prompt_prologue: First, load the Recording Rig Bridge tools (rig_checkpoint, rig_turn_end) so they are available. Do the task below; immediately after the file exists call the rig_checkpoint tool with name "wrote-shared"; and as your final step call the rig_turn_end tool.
steps.command: Create the file /tmp/rig-tiers-demo/shared-fact.txt containing the single line 'meeting at 0900', then confirm it exists. In one sentence, note that this is a host-filesystem fact (it lives on disk). Then state one session-only thought you will deliberately NOT write to any file — a scratch note that exists only in this Code session.

steps.system_prompt_prologue: First, load the Recording Rig Bridge tools (rig_checkpoint, rig_turn_end) so they are available. Answer the request below; right before finishing call the rig_checkpoint tool with name "narrated"; and as your final step call the rig_turn_end tool.
steps.command: In two or three sentences: you are the Chat surface and have no filesystem access, so you cannot read the shared-fact.txt the Code surface just wrote. Explain that a shared knowledge tier (like Nexus T2/T3) WOULD carry that fact across every surface, whereas a session-local scratch note (T1) stays only where it was written.

Read the file /tmp/rig-tiers-demo/shared-fact.txt and report exactly what it contains. If you cannot reach it from here, say so plainly and briefly — that boundary IS the point of this demo: a shared tier (Nexus T2/T3) would carry the fact across this sandbox even though the raw host filesystem does not.
